security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context-switches sstatus (and vsstatus for KVM) without saving/restoring the CRGE bit, or initializes thread sstatus without clearing CRGE to a known value. When CRGE leaks between processes with different Svucrg expectations, one process runs with PTE.{CRW,CD,CRG} interpreted under Svucrg semantics while its page tables were built under the plain CHERI vmem semantics (or vice versa).
security_spec.summary: CRGE is a per-thread enable bit that redefines PTE capability semantics; if the kernel fails to context-switch it, a thread may execute under unintended Svucrg semantics causing spurious capability-store traps (Svade) or silent hardware CD dirty-tracking (Svadu) on pages not prepared for it.
